title: MongoDB
description: A document-oriented NoSQL database that stores data in flexible, JSON-like BSON documents, offering high scalability and flexible schemas.

title: Service
description: A layer or component that encapsulates business logic and workflow rules, mediating operations between controllers and data access.

title: Testing
description: The practice of verifying and validating that software functions correctly, satisfies requirements, and prevents regressions.

title: Test Driven Development
description: A development practice where automated tests are written before the code itself, following a rapid Red-Green-Refactor cycle.

title: Services
description: Independent, loosely coupled software units or subsystems providing distinct capabilities across a network or distributed system.

title: Controllers
description: Components in MVC architectures that handle incoming HTTP requests, coordinate business logic, and select responses to return.

title: Monolith
description: An architectural pattern where all business logic, data access, and user interfaces are packaged and deployed as a single unit.

title: API
description: Application Programming Interface: A contract defining how software components interact and exchange structured data.

title: HTTP Endpoints
description: Target URLs or routes exposed by an application or web API where clients send requests (GET, POST, etc.) to perform operations.

title: Microservices
description: An architectural approach structuring an application as a suite of small, independently deployable services around business domains.

title: Modules
description: Self-contained units of code with distinct boundaries and public interfaces that help organize and decouple large systems.

title: Role Based Authentication
description: A security mechanism (RBAC) controlling user access to resources and operations based on assigned system roles and privileges.

title: OWASP
description: Open Worldwide Application Security Project: A community dedicated to providing guidelines and tools to secure web applications.

title: Accessibility
description: Designing and developing software usable by everyone, including people relying on assistive technologies (a11y).

title: DRY
description: Don't Repeat Yourself: A software principle stating that every piece of knowledge must have a single, unambiguous representation.

title: Views
description: The presentation layer in MVC that renders models and user interface elements for display to the end user.

title: Models
description: The component in MVC that manages application state, data structures, and core domain business rules.

title: MVC
description: Model-View-Controller: A foundational architectural pattern separating data representation, user interface, and input handling.

title: Ubiquitous Language
description: A core Domain-Driven Design concept establishing a common, rigorous language shared by developers and domain experts in code and speech.

title: MVCS
description: Model-View-Controller-Service: An evolution of MVC introducing a dedicated Service layer to keep business logic out of controllers.

title: Persistence
description: The mechanism allowing application data to outlive the process that created it, typically through databases or file storage.

title: Components
description: Reusable, modular software elements encapsulating specific behavior and state, communicating through established interfaces.

title: Boundaries
description: Architectural divisions between subsystems, modules, or layers that protect domain rules from infrastructure and external concerns.

title: Martin Fowler
description: Renowned software author and Chief Scientist at ThoughtWorks, famous for pioneering works on refactoring, patterns, and architecture.

title: Uncle Bob
description: Robert C. Martin: Celebrated software craftsman and author who popularized the SOLID principles, Clean Architecture, and Clean Code.
